answers.answer: For each held office card, roll one die simultaneously; add 1 per fatigue on that card, and the Chairman adds 1. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move the retiree to Pensioners, flip the office card into Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal office attrition.

evidence.quote: **Attrition:** Simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal office attrition.

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner select a card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties break by most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. They may take or discard one; chosen/discarded cards are not replaced during selection, and if display empties remaining eligible players are skipped. At the end discard all remaining cards and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if no one took a card. Return unused pensioners to supplies.

evidence.quote: **Prestige:** Players who retired at least one pensioner must each take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties: most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. Acting player may peek at display blackmails. **Do not replace a chosen/discarded card during selection. If the display becomes empty, immediately skip every remaining eligible player.** Finish the display step by **discarding all remaining cards and refilling exactly three: prestige faceup, blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card**. Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies.

answers.answer: At phase start check whether the opportunity marker already matches the selected main action; if so, that main action may be taken twice. Then move the marker to the chosen main action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action afterward; it is never doubled and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices and marker already on Enlist Writer, the doubled action places two writers, plus the vacancy bonus of one additional writer once this turn: three total.

evidence.summary_location: Family — opportunity marker and extra action; Enlist Writer
evidence.quote: 1. Check where your opportunity marker was **at phase start** (it begins off the board). 2. Choose a main family action: take it once, or **may take it twice if the marker already matched it**. 3. **Place/move the opportunity marker onto your chosen main action.** 4. After the main action, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant its extra action. This extra action is never doubled by the marker and never moves the marker.

answers.answer: After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one; repeat while both remain. If Debt is zero, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order. Applicants become Company shares only upon moving into Court. Seeking a share pays the bank, never Company treasuries.

evidence.quote: **New Company shares:** After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one. Repeat while both remain. Pieces in Court are Company shares. With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order. Seeking a share never pays family cash into Company treasuries.

answers.answer: Fill vacancies in ascending number on card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate. Hiring your own family into an ordinary office requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool. Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. On promotion, transfer fatigue to the new card and insert the old card, vacant, in ascending hiring order. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip it; the office stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

evidence.quote: Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that member into the office; its owner gets the card. When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert its old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. If no candidate exists, or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

answers.answer: Shareholders elect: former Chairman first announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half current shares); any shareholder may campaign, and the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. If nobody reaches it, former Chairman chooses any shareholder including self, with no Nepotism consent. The winner’s Company share moves to Chairman slot but still counts as a share for dividends, majority, and scoring; it cannot be traded or invested in firms.

evidence.quote: **Chairman election:** Former Chairman first announces **the number of shares needed for a pure majority** (more than half of current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one winner’s Company shares into Chairman slot and give title marker. It still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms. If no candidate gets support, former Chairman picks any shareholder including self; no Nepotism consent.

answers.answer: For a Company-office check, first commit resources and pay all check cash from that acting office’s treasury to the bank; gather dice and subtract penalties, then roll and use the lowest die. 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may retry if resources and office limits permit; 5–6 is catastrophic: no more office actions, return officeholder to supply, discard fatigue, and flip card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm procedures can modify this. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success.

evidence.quote: **Success checks (p17):** First commit resources/cash: **all cash for a Company-office check comes from that acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank**. Gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll. Use lowest die: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure, retry if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 catastrophic failure, no more office actions, return officeholder to supply, discard fatigue and flip card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm procedures modify this. You cannot take a dead action with no effect or chance of success

answers.answer: Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each increasing Balance by £5. Each additional advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares (Chairman counts), and Debt may never pass the track end. Then allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, lowering Balance by each transfer; may interleave borrowing and allocation while respecting limits. Money already in office treasuries stays there.

evidence.quote: May add up to three Debt freely, each +£5 Balance. Each additional advance requires consent of players controlling majority Company shares (Chairman counts); never pass Debt track end. Then **allocate all Balance** to other offices’ treasuries, lowering Balance by each transfer. May interleave borrowing and allocation while respecting total borrowing rules. Cash already in offices remains there for their use.

answers.answer: Manager of Shipping must spend until £2 or less remains. Lease an extra ship for £2; fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without owner consent; buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Place acquired ships in any sea zone, including China once created. Extra ships return to supply at Refresh.

evidence.quote: Must spend treasury until **£2 or less remains**. Lease extra ship £2; fit ship from shipyard £3 without owner consent; buy Company ship £5 **only if no ships remain on shipyards**. Place each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once office exists. Extra ships serve only until Refresh.

answers.answer: Declare home plus only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 of President treasury buys one die; subtract one per declared nonhome region. A successful President Trade fills at most one order per ship in that Presidency sea zone, without exhausting ships. First writer goes to home port; each later order extends the route filled during that same Trade. Other Presidency writers cannot extend it. Writers do not cap capacity: use them all, then filled-order tokens for remaining ships. A President cannot fill another President’s home region even if vacant. Company Balance gets printed revenue, or half rounded down for an order firms already filled; President gets £1/order and writer owners £1/writer. At most one successful Trade per President/turn.

evidence.quote: Declare regions for Trade: include home region, and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 President’s treasury buys one die; subtract one per declared nonhome region. Failure can be retried during operations if affordable; catastrophe removes President. At most **one successful Trade per President per turn**.

answers.answer: A Commander may target their own Presidency home, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region; not another home or another Presidency’s Company region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order to make the action meaningful. Exhaust each chosen officer/regiment for one die, each local alliance for its printed dice; subtract the combined strength of the target and all other regions in its empire (target counted once; Company defense is zero). A noncatastrophic failure may retry with remaining resources. After every attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll officer losses.

evidence.quote: 1. Target own Presidency’s home, any associated region, or any region bordering an associated region. Cannot target another home region or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region. Company region must have unrest or a closed order to give action an effect. 2. Exhaust chosen officers/regiments to bottom for one die each and local alliances for printed dice. Subtract the combined strength of target and **all other regions in its empire, counting target only once**. Company-controlled defense strength is zero. Roll normal check; a noncatastrophic failure can retry using remaining resources. 3. After **each attempt**, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in attempt; each 6 returns an officer to supply. Regiments never roll officer losses.

answers.answer: On success take bank loot of £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, minimum surviving participating officers this attempt +1. Payout cycles give Commander family £1 for Commander plus £1 per used surviving own officer; then clockwise other families £1 per used surviving officer; bank last £1 per used regiment and alliance piece. On catastrophe, Commander returns half own family’s trophies rounded up and member to supply; exhausted officers still roll losses.

evidence.quote: On success, take loot from the bank: **£4 per target tower + faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of (surviving officers used in this attempt + 1)**. answers.answer: Use the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls current pool without penalty, then reduces pool by one regardless. Success pays £1, or £2 if immediately preceding roll failed, then choose exactly one: build one ship stage, commission one regiment to President’s Army, or tax £2 to Balance or President treasury (unsplit). Each tax after first this turn adds regional unrest. Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest; catastrophe also removes officeholder. Continue with shrinking pool until stop, no dice, or catastrophe.

evidence.quote: Take the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one **regardless of result**.

answers.answer: Company expenses are £1 per existing Debt, each Army officer/regiment, and each sea-zone ship including China (not Commanders). If Balance is short, take £5 loans; each raises Debt only if track space remains, and at max Debt continue taking loans without further Debt advance. New Debt adds no current-turn expense; set Balance to zero after loans. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance to expectations at current Standing and lower Standing one if short; then Chairman may pay affordable dividends at £1 per Company share. Advance Standing only if total dividend cash is strictly greater than expectations.

evidence.quote: If insufficient, take £5 emergency loans. Each loan advances Debt one **only while a track space remains**. **At maximum Debt, keep taking loans without advancing Debt any further.** Newly added emergency Debt causes no extra current-turn expense. After using emergency loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower Standing two.

answers.answer: Resolve primary Crisis first, then secondary rebellions in every other Company region with unrest, in Bombay→Madras→Bengal Army order; each Commander sets order of associated regions. Primary normal Crisis strength is its usual attack strength plus target unrest; primary Foreign Invasion uses only its ordinary die; each secondary Rebellion uses only that region’s unrest cubes. Defense is chosen by associated Commander; if vacant Military Affairs acts, and if both vacant Chairman chooses. Exhaust active Army pieces equal to strength or as many as possible. Equal newly exhausted strength defeats attack, clears all target unrest, gives actual Commander one trophy (substitutes no trophies); if normal primary Invasion, remove one attacker tower if possible. Non-equal means attack succeeds and Region Loss; successful primary Invasion also applies empire growth.

evidence.summary_location: Events in India — Attacks on Company and mounting defense
evidence.quote: An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve attacks in this order: **primary Crisis first**, then secondary regions in **Bombay → Madras → Bengal** Army order. **Within each Presidency, that Commander chooses the order of its associated regions.**

answers.answer: Support −1 or lower fails: discard law, resolve dilemma If Failed text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial; new PM shifts proposed policy one adjacent space either direction and resolves it. Support zero or higher passes: keep law among passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve selected policy first, then immediate law effects. Restore all used vote cards afterward either way. If law causes failure, finish vote before scoring.

evidence.quote: -1 or less fails: discard law, resolve dilemma’s If Failed text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial; new PM moves proposed policy one space either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. Zero or higher passes: place law with passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve selected policy **then** immediate law effects. **Finally restore every card used for voting to its regular orientation**, after either outcome.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, before London Season, PM may call special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space; must call if either is on a starred space. Use ordinary voting/support threshold, but no policy accompanies vote and PM may vote against. Pass: lower Debt one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, PM takes passed-law token, activate firms. Fail: raise Company-share scoring value with Court token up to ±3 VP/share; PM remains in power and Deregulation law is not discarded. 1813 starts deregulated.

evidence.quote: In 1758/Long 1710, at turn start before London Season, PM **may** call special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt on lined space, and **must** if either on starred space. Use the ordinary voting procedure and support threshold. **No policy accompanies this vote, and PM may vote against it.**

answers.answer: To form a firm, a player managing none returns one eligible Company share to supply or flips a workshop to invested side, flips family board to charter, places a family member as first share, sets value cube to leftmost space and takes £5 from bank to London treasury. Invest with manager consent using same contribution; bank adds £5 to London. Maximum 10 shares; later investments still add £5 but no share. Cannot use Chairman share; Company shares prohibited when Standing and/or Debt on lined space; cannot invest shares created this turn. Invested workshops never revert and lose bonus/failure VP.

evidence.quote: **Form a firm — only if you currently manage none:** return one eligible Company share to supply or flip workshop to invested side. **Flip your family board to its firm-charter side**, then place a family member as first firm share, set value cube to leftmost track space and take £5 from bank into the London treasury.

answers.answer: Each firm gets exactly one attempt per turn and needs at least one ship; may choose closed home port, but selected home must be open when filled. Managers secretly choose strategy and London bid; Hobnob means no bid/trade/dividends. Reveal bids simultaneously; reveal strategies at matching Presidency before actions, roll one die per bid £ and pay bid bank; any 1/2 permits trade. Initiative is ships minus successful dice. After President’s successful Trade, lowest initiative fills first; President chooses ties. If President vacant or never succeeds, firms act after Commander/Governors and Chairman resolves ties. Fill open orders up to ships+1 from home, tracing own route; cannot refill own earlier order, may refill another firm/Company order at half listed revenue rounded down. Value advances once per full £6 added to India treasury.

evidence.quote: At beginning of associated Presidency’s operations, before any actions, matching firms reveal strategy and roll one die per committed £1, paying bid to bank. At least one 1/2 permits trade. Firm initiative = ship count minus number of successful dice (1s/2s); it can be negative. President’s successful Trade creates initiative the same way using Presidency ships.

answers.answer: At Revenue start firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm Value, from either/both firm treasuries. If unable, dissolve unless rescued by normal-rule emergency investments or emergency negotiated merger; insolvent dissolution sends shares to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships to matching shipyards and charter to family side; workshops stay invested. After expenses manager may pay dividends from India treasury only: each pays £1/share plus £1 manager. A shareholder may waive only with manager consent. Record actual total cash paid on Company Balance track; active non-Hobnob firm paying none marks zero, Hobnob retains prior marker. Sweep remaining India cash to London.

evidence.quote: At start Revenue before Company, firms act in initiative order then other firms; ties by manager’s most windows then PM clockwise order. Pay £1 per charter ship **plus higher of share count or firm value**; can use either/both treasuries.

answers.answer: Components are limited; if a supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice, and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP, and Vote tracks are unlimited. All information, including discards and family cash, is public except facedown blackmail and firm strategies/bids temporarily concealed during selection.

evidence.quote: **Limits:** Components are limited: when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. All information, including discards and family cash, is public except facedown blackmail and temporarily concealed firm strategies/bids during selection.

answers.answer: Negotiable: enterprises, facedown blackmail, family cash, Company/firm shares, promise cards. Not negotiable: officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial, Chairman piece. Transfer a share by returning old owner’s family member and replacing it at same location with receiving family’s member. Blackmail must remain facedown when traded; once played faceup it cannot be traded.

Future-behavior promises are nonbinding except a printed promise card’s guaranteed effect may be called if possible; follow its timing/limits, and no promise calls during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which. Transferred resources cannot activate twice (e.g., workshop bonus cannot pay twice after same-phase sale).

answers.answer: Use the scenario player setup cards; add three extra cards for five players or six for six, then shuffle and deal evenly. Place every listed holding: cash and enterprise cards, each office member/card, Company-share members in Court, writers/officers/trainees in indicated locations, Commanders in Army slots without office cards, ships in listed sea zones or on shipyards if unfitted. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together into one deck; deal three display cards, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown.

evidence.quote: Use that scenario’s player setup cards; add three extra cards for five players or six for six players. Shuffle and deal evenly. **Place every listed holding:** take cash from the bank and enterprise cards into your area; put each office’s family member in its office and give its matching office card to that owner; put Company-share members in Court of Directors; put writers, officers and trainees in their indicated Presidency/Army/Training boxes; put a Commander in that Army’s Commander slot **without an office card**; take each shipyard and put its matching ship in the **listed sea zone**, or **on its shipyard if unfitted**. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP.

answers.answer: Game ends after scenario’s final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Normally failure is immediate; if during Events, finish that phase; if legislation causes failure, finish the vote. After game over stop negotiations, promise calls, and blackmail unless a card explicitly allows final-scoring use; during all Final Scoring no negotiations or promise calls.

evidence.quote: The game ends after scenario’s final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Normally failure is immediate; failure during Events finishes that phase, and legislation failure finishes vote before scoring. Once game over, stop negotiations, calling promises and playing blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use. **During all of Final Scoring, no negotiations or promise calls are allowed.**

answers.answer: Power counts enterprises and Company shares at current Power-track rates (bottom two positions zero), plus 1 per passed-law token and trophy, 2 for PM, and printed card power (blackmail faceup or facedown, applicable spouse). Most/second awards by final turn: 3/1 VP for turns 1–3, 5/2 for 4–6, 8/4 for 7–8. Tied first gets only lower award each; no other award. Tied second gets none. evidence.quote: **Power award:** Count **enterprises and Company shares**, using their current Power-track rates (bottom two positions zero), +1 per passed-law token and trophy, +2 for PM, plus printed card power (blackmail faceup or down, applicable spouse). Most/second awards are **3/1 VP if final turn 1–3, 5/2 if turn 4–6, 8/4 if turn 7–8**. Tied first: only lower award to each tied player; no other award. Tied second receive none.

answers.answer: Surviving Company: add current Court VP value per Company share. Failed Company: subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop; scores can be negative. If survived, final scoring has office attrition then retire Pensioners, no display cards; if failed draw one random Company failure card instead. Final turn firm special retirement, when deregulated, remains available whether Company survived or failed.

evidence.quote: **Court/workshops:** If Company survived, add Court’s current VP per Company share. If failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Scores may be negative.

answers.answer: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions, and cannot be transferred; taking one may require immediate enterprise/share trades. answers.answer: Director may make repeated Special Envoy checks, paying £1 treasury per die, no penalty.
